we show that large-scale graphene crystals grown by CVD can be transferred on arbitrary substrates and exhibit the same electronic transport properties of exfoliated graphene crystals, with the advantage of being compatible with industrial processes.

the development of a large-scale approach to graphene production that yields single-layer graphene with remarkable electronic properties.

the development of scalable methods for graphene production, with the characterization of the resulting crystals, and with the demonstration of the feasibility to fabricate devices on the basis of these materials.
the development of a large-scale approach for the production of single-layer graphene with outstanding electronic properties, comparable with those of micro-mechanically produced graphene.

the graphene we produce is the most ideal material ever measured in a device.

graphene, grown by CVD, is a technology-ready material.

the graphene crystals we produce are as good as the ones exfoliated from bulk graphite, but on a much larger scale.
we have shown that the large-scale approach can yield graphene crystals with transport properties as good as the state-of-the-art.

the CVD approach to graphene, when coupled with the polymer-mediated semi-dried transfer, can produce high-quality crystals, which are ideal for electronic transport studies and technological application.

the CVD-grown graphene crystals, despite their large size, can be used to probe the fundamental properties of graphene and, at the same time, are suitable for technological application.
